question: The constant presence of Turkish fishing vessels in the Cyclades is not simply an issue affecting fisheries – it a matter of national sovereignty and violation of the maritime borders of Greece and therefore of the EU itself. The failure to respond or exercise any substantial supervision encourages Turkish aggression and leaves Greek fishermen unprotected.1 In view of the above, the Commission is asked: 1.
Does it consider that the entry of Turkish fishing vessels into Greek territorial waters constitutes an infringement of European fishing policy and the national sovereignty of a Member State?
What supervisory and preventive measures are being implemented in the Cyclades area by FRONTEX or other European mechanisms?
How will immediate support be provided to local Greek communities and professional fishermen who are affected by unfair competition and the lack of protection?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.10.2025) 1. The EU has a strategic interest in a stable and secure environment in the Mediterranean and continues to expect that all countries respect the jurisdiction, sovereignty and sovereign rights of all Member States, in accordance with international law, including the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).

Additionally, according to UNCLOS and customary international law, coastal States have sovereignty over their territorial sea, including for the adoption of laws and regulations related to fishing, innocent passage as well as to take the necessary steps to prevent non-innocent passage. 2. The European Fisheries Control Agency deploys a patrol vessel on a permanent basis in the Mediterranean.

Its activities may be complemented by aircraft and satellite monitoring and support activities to national authorities if requested. 3. The Greek European Maritime Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) programme provides key support for the resilience and competitiveness of the fisheries sector and coastal communities.

It supports modernisation and innovation to boost market competitiveness, training related to sustainable and innovative practices and projects aimed at diversifying income. A significant portion of the funds is allocated to fisheries control and enforcement, including enhancing surveillance of fishing activity and traceability, as well as addressing illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing.

The Member States’ Managing Authorities may select for support operations under the scope, priorities and specific objectives of their national EMFAF programme and in line with applicable Union and national law. The Commission works with Greece to ensure its EMFAF programme meets sector-specific needs.
